title: Track the SLA Timers
subtitle: Per-priority clocks and breach flags
scenario: It is 4:30 PM. The day's tickets are routed. Track each one's SLA: the target depends on its priority, and a breach flag says whether the clock ran out. On a clean day nothing breached - but the flags still have to be set.
input:
SLA targets by priority: P1 = 15 min, P3 = 8 hours, P4 = 2 days.
Today: TKT-4001 (P1) escalated at 2:14, resolved 2:40 - within 15 min. TKT-4002 (P3) worked well within 8 hours. TKT-4003 (P4) within 2 days.
Record each ticket's SLA target and breach flag (no for all today).
instructions: Write one row per ticket: TKT-4001, TKT-4002, TKT-4003.
Set each slaTarget from its priority (15 min, 8 hours, 2 days).
Set breachFlag to no for all (clean day).
Return a JSON array of the three rows, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build a JSON array of SLA rows for TKT-4001 (P1, 15 min), TKT-4002 (P3, 8 hours), TKT-4003 (P4, 2 days). Each has ticketId, slaTarget, breachFlag (no for all today).
successMessage: SLA tracked. Each ticket has its per-priority target and a breach flag the digest reads.
editorHelper: Target comes from priority; breach flag says if the clock ran out.

sections.title: Time is a priority-scaled signal
sections.body: A P1 clock is minutes; a P4 is days. The SLA target comes from the priority, so the same 'is it late?' question means very different things per ticket.

sections.title: A flag needs a target
sections.body: A breach flag only means something against a target. Recording both - the target and whether it was met - is what makes the digest's breach count auditable.

sections.title: Clean days still get tracked
sections.body: Today nothing breached, but the flags are set to 'no' anyway. Tracking is not just for fires; the clean baseline is what makes a breach visible when it happens.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: SLA rows the digest totals into a breach count and load-shedding acts on when a queue runs hot.

fieldGuide.meaning: The SLA target from the priority.
fieldGuide.hint: P1 15 min, P3 8 hours, P4 2 days.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd set a due time per ticket based on its priority and flag any that blew past it.

tools.powerAutomate: compute due = created + SLA(priority); flag if now > due
tools.zapier: a delay/deadline per priority with a breach tag

takeaway.heading: SLA tracked
points: You set each ticket's SLA target from its priority.
Breach flags are recorded against those targets, so they are auditable.
A clean day still gets tracked - the baseline makes breaches visible.
The digest reads these rows for its breach count.
The workflow can now measure every ticket against its per-priority clock.
